IX.     YOUTH  HOSTELS
           The Committee is surprised to see that due to overall reduction of Ministry’s allocation, share of this
scheme was drastically reduced from Rs. 260 lakh to just  Rs. 60 lakh. This general reduction in Ministry’s
allocation, committee feels, should have been evenly spread to the other schemes as well.       
                                                                                                                                             (Para 9.2)
           The Committee notes that performance of this scheme is not satisfactory, in view of the expenditure
pattern in the entire Ninth Plan period as well as 2003-04. The fact that the allocation of the Ministry was
reduced from Rs. 260 lakhs to 60 lakhs last year, gives an impression that this scheme was not given the
priority that it deserved. Just 85 youth Hostels upto December 2003, in a country of continental dimensions, the
Committee feels, is highly inadequate which needs to be increased in the coming years. The Committee notes that
the spread of these 85 hostels state-wise is also highly uneven. In view of this, the Committee recommends that
the Ministry must try to see that this scheme picks up and gets adequate resources so that the pending
projects are completed in time. It is also necessary to fix physical targets for this scheme every year.(Para 9.4)
           The Committee feels that this scheme lacks adequate publicity, as a result, youth, particularly from
rural areas, were not able to make use of hostel facilities. The Committee,  therefore, is of the opinion
that existence of youth hostel facilities should be given wide publicity particularly by Akashvani
which has large audience in rural areas. It also recommends to strengthen the scheme as the present coverage of
the scheme was too less to show any impact.                                                                   (Para 9.5)
           The Committee does not know how much of the existing facility of youth hostels was being
utilized by the women youth. Generally women, particularly from rural areas, do not come out due to reasons of
security and safety. The Committee, therefore, recommends that separate girls hostels should also be constructed
on the lines of youth hostel.                                                                                                          (Para 9.6)
X.      NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR YOUTH
           The Committee gets an impression from what has been stated above that the Commission was not taken
with due seriousness although it had laudable mandate. Its initial tenure of six months, the Committee feels, was
not realistic and the Commission was not provided with the necessary wherewithal and assistance for starting its
work in time. The Committee disapproves this ad-hocism as also the manner in which funds were arranged first
by re-appropriation and then from the Contingency Fund. The Commission has since submitted its report after
two years and four months which it was to submit within 6 months initially. The Committee expresses its
unhappiness at the manner everything was done. However, it would like to have a note on the report of the
Commission at the earliest.                                                                                                                             (Para 10.2)
XI.     ASSISTANCE TO RURAL YOUTH AND SPORTS CLUB
        The  Committee is at a loss to understand as to how the Ministry would be able to meet this
target with the present allocation. In view of the scheme being rural youth-oriented, its importance can
hardly be overemphasized.  The Committee, therefore, urges the Ministry to make efforts for
obtaining  adequate resources so that the momentum of the scheme is not lost.                                                 
(Para 11.2)
           The Committee further notes that this is a merged scheme, among others, the scheme for research,

152nd Report of Committee on HRD
file:///D/Committee%20on%20HRD/152ndreport.htm[01-07-2016 15:21:26]
evaluation and publication. In the absence of any  mention about these aspects in the new scheme, it
appears that the evaluation and publicity aspects have been given a go by. It is very unfortunate. The Ministry
should have a permanent mechanism for evaluation and publicity of its schemes.      (Para 11.3)
XII.   NEW SCHEMES
           The Committee finds it appalling that the funds are being allocated for the scheme for welfare and
development of Adolescents for the last three financial years but these went unspent every year mainly because
the scheme could not be finalized. Similar was the story of the proposed scheme of  Establishment of
National/State Youth Centres. In this case also the amount  allocated since 2002-03, remained
unutilized again because this scheme also  could not be finalized till today. This reflects lack of
foresight and planning in the Ministry. The Committee deprecates this tendency of allocating amounts even when
the schemes were not finalized. This is against the norms of fiscal discipline. The Committee, therefore,
feels that Ministry should ask for allocations only after the finalization of  the schemes. It, therefore,
recommends that these two schemes should be finalized and implemented without further delay and ensure that
funds provided are fully utilized.                                                                                      (Para 12.2)
XIII.   RAJIV GANDHI NATIONAL INSTITUTE FOR YOUTH DEVELOPMENT
           The Committee notes with concern the pace of development of the Institute including the construction
work which is going of on at a very slow speed. The Committee also notes that even the required
complement of academic & other staff were also not in place so far. The construction was held up due to dispute
with the contractor. In view of the importance of the mandate of the Institute in the area of youth development,
the Committee recommends that all efforts be made to ensure that RGNIYD was provided with faculty and other
staff to enable it to fulfill its mandated function and objectives. Initiatives also be taken to provide the physical
infrastructure required for this premier Institute as early as possible.                         (Para 13.2)
XIV.   NON GOVERNMENT ORGANISATIONS (NGOs)
           Committee appreciates the good work done by several NGOs it however feels concerned to note that such
large number of NGOs have failed to submit utilization certificates for years together. The Committee further
notes that even then some NGOs were given funds for the subsequent years also. The Committee is not aware of
the circumstances under which grants were released even without UCs given by them. The Committee would like
to know the action taken, if any, against all the defaulting NGOs and the steps proposed/taken for ensuring
timely submission of UCs by them. The Committee feels that extra care should be taken while selecting NGOs for
giving grants and the Ministry should not shy away from taking deterrent action against the erring ones. The
Ministry should have a mechanism to have a regular monitoring of the performance of the NGOs, including
physical inspection.                                                                                                                         (Para 14.2)
XV.    SPORTS AND PHYSICAL EDUCATION
           While appreciating the need for the additional funds to the Ministry, the Committee would like to point
out that the Tenth Plan outlay of Rs. 1145.36 crores is more than double the amount of Rs. 472.61 crores
outlay of Ninth Plan. The Committee feels that with this increased allocation, the Ministry should be able to
make up for the gap to some extent between the allocation and its requirement. But it would certainly not be
enough to fulfill the objectives of extending  NSS and creating proper sports facilities in every school. The
Committee recommends that the proposal of the Ministry  regarding getting the additional funds from
the education cess be seriously considered as these projects would benefit ultimately schools only which are
primarily the responsibility of the Ministry of HRD.                                                     (Para 15.5)
        The  Department, however, should concentrate on making an assessment of all those sports
related schemes which are not performing well and take corrective measures wherever required.        
                                                                                                                                           (Para 15.6)
XVI.   SPORTS AUTHORITY OF INDIA
(i)      Budgetary Allocation
           The committee, however, observes that in 2003-04 BE allocation of Rs. 110.50 crores had to be reduced to
Rs. 98.50 crores in RE, whereas actual expenditure was only Rs. 97.00 crores. The Committee feels that the pace
of expenditure of the SAI allocations does not present an encouraging picture. The Committee would like the
Ministry to ensure optimum utilization of funds by the SAI for its programmes in 2004-05.(Para 16.3)
(ii)      SAI Sub-Centres

152nd Report of Committee on HRD
file:///D/Committee%20on%20HRD/152ndreport.htm[01-07-2016 15:21:26]
        The  Committee finds that the SAI Regional Centres at Sonepat, Gandhinagar, Bhopal, Kolkata,
Imphal and Bangalore are not evenly distributed as regards different regions in the country. So is the case with
the sub-centres also. The Committee feels that the creation of the regional as well as sub-centres should be based
on performance of the region as well as the States. It appears that this has not been the case so far.         (Para
16.4)
           The Committee recommends that the construction work at sub-centre at Hazaribagh may be
completed at the earliest. State government should be persuaded to hand over the land at a suitable place
so that the construction of Sub Centre at Nagercoil could be initiated without further loss of time.(Para 16.5)
(iii)      Scheme for Dope Test
           Last few years have seen a number of sportspersons specially the weightlifters and athletes testing positive
for banned drugs. These instances have brought shame instead of fame to the Nation. Our Scheme for Dope test
was launched only three years ago. The SAI has anti-doping lab set up a decade ago in New Delhi, it has still not
acquired the requisite international certification to gain legal sanctity. So, even if anybody fails a test, he or she
can successfully challenge it in a Court. Such a situation allows the over-ambitious ones to take the easy
route.           (Para 16.6)
           In view of cases in Athens Olympics and earlier experiences, the Committee notes that our weightlifters
are most hit by the scourge of doping. Every time an Indian contingent prepares to leave the country for a mega
event, doping tests are hastily conducted and surprisingly they do not test positive here but fail the test in
International events.                                                                                                                               (Para 16.7)
        The  Committee was surprised to know that nobody seems to take the responsibility for the same.
Even the Sports Ministry and SAI claim that it is not their duty to conduct dope tests on athletes who are
under control of  IOA and various federations. Federations have a ready-excuse about the high cost
of conducting dope test. Thus, at the end of the day nobody is ready to  own the responsibility for the
bad name that a few athletes bring to the nation.
                                                                                                                                           (Para 16.8)
           The Committee feels extremely unhappy about the continuing indifference shown by all sports bodies - the
Ministry, IOA, Federations and the SAI about the serious malaise. They appear to be passing the buck to each
other and no serious attempt has been made so far by them to clean the mess that has plagued our sports
persons.              (Para 16.9)
           The very fact that sportsperson after having been cleared by our test, get caught during the events shows
how rudimentary or outdated procedure we adopt about this testing. It means lab at SAI does not have the
necessary facility for this test. The Committee was informed that the procedure allows for tempering of the
samples also.                                                                                                                  (Para 16.10)
           The Committee, therefore, recommends that more sports scientists should be deputed by SAI to efficiently
put all sportspersons to dope testing. It should evolve some mechanism so that the samples could not be
tempered. The entire procedure should be transparent and the punishment has to be  as per
international norms. Though there is a provision for withdrawal of grants and facilities to the offender, but
that of course, is rarely resorted to. The Coaches and doctors of Sportspersons testing positive should be made
liable because during the training they are in-charge of their trainees. Blaming the sportsperson alone will not be
fair.(Para 16.11)
        The  Committee recommends that the Ministry should make efforts to streamline the procedure
for Dope testing, upgrading the test facilities, employing experts in the area for making the test results foolproof.
Involving many agencies in this, Committee feels, would only complicate the  matter. Only SAI and
IOA, therefore, should be made responsible for this work. And they should put necessary guidelines in tune with
World Anti-Doping Code.                                                                                                          (Para 16.12)
           The Committee also emphasizes an urgent need for educating our athletes, coaches and other supporting
personnel about the harmful effects of dope; conducting in-competition and out-of-competition dope tests on
sportspersons; and promoting research and training in the area.                               (Para 16.13)
(iv)     Scouting and Nurturing talents
           The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that performance of these schemes should be
evaluated and problem identified with a view to strengthening and expanding them to more and
more areas of the  country. These schemes be implemented with full vigour so as to bring out our talented

152nd Report of Committee on HRD
file:///D/Committee%20on%20HRD/152ndreport.htm[01-07-2016 15:21:26]
children and youth to the forefront.                                                                               (Para 16.15)
           The Committee agrees with the Ministry that sporting standards in country have not declined. It,
however, believes that it cannot be said to have  improved either. Our performance in international
sports is not at all  satisfactory and commensurate with the size of our country as well as the
population.           (Para 16.16)
        The  Committee is of the opinion that training is the core aspect of good performance.
Rigorous training for years together for producing champions is required. The Committee opines that
sports training should be properly planned and managed for getting the best results. The Committee
recommends scientific training modules for our sportsperson in different 
disciplines after consulting coaches, federations and experts in fields like sports medicine and sports
psychology.           (Para 16.17)
           The overall performance as well as functioning of the SAI, the Committee  feels, has been far
from satisfactory. Our performance in international sports as it is, is highly disappointing. The SAI
obviously  has not been able to make any significant impact as was initially visualised when it was set up. It
is said to have developed into an unwieldy bureaucratic organization which is not being managed by
sportspersons themselves. The Committee feels that there is a need to have a re-look on both its mandate as well
as organization with a view to bringing in this organization professionalism, dynamism and efficiency so that it
becomes a think tank in the sports arena.                                                                                                (Para 16.19)
XVII.GRANTS FOR CREATION OF SPORTS INFRASTRUCTURE
        The  Committee is happy to see that different schemes of infrastructural support  have been
proposed to be clubbed under two umbrella schemes on the pattern as was done for the schemes of
promotion of sports Awards incentives. The Committee feels that it would enable the Ministry to have a focussed
and effective implementation of scheme to create infrastructure  of a high standard in various parts
of the country. The Committee emphasizes the need for special focus on developing playgrounds in
villages and providing sports equipments to rural youth.                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                           (Para 17.5)
XVIII.  GRANTS FOR PROMOTION OF SPORTS IN UNIVERSITIES AND COLLEGES
        The  Committee observes that allocation as well as expenditure under this scheme has increased
over the years due to receipt of more and more proposals. It was able to utilize 
Rs. 32.78 crores as against Rs. 23.11 crores allocated during the Ninth Plan. The Committee urges the Ministry to
see that proposals received were processed and grant released within minimum possible time so that pace of its
implementation is not broken. The Committee  is, however, not satisfied with the coverage of colleges and
universities under the scheme. It appears that proposals are coming from a few States, its benefit, therefore, are
not reaching to other States. The Ministry should take upon the responsibility of encouraging
universities/colleges from the areas where from the proposals are less or are not coming at all.                 (Para
18.3)
XIX.   GRANTS FOR INSTALLATION OF SYNTHETIC PLAYING SURFACES
        The Committee notes with serious concern that the decrease during these years was due to non-
receipt of accounts and required documents from the grantees. The Committee is apprehensive whether the
allocation for 2004-05 will also be utilized. As per the trend during the previous years, it appears difficult, if not
impossible. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry must try and get all the pending UCs and
documents cleared before the close of the financial year. In view of large number of pending UCs and non-
completion of required documents, the Committee feels, there is apparently some problem in the formalities to be
completed by the grantees. The Committee feels that this is a strong case for review, with a view to resolving the
problems. The Committee would like to be apprised about the number of projects completed under the scheme
during the last three years (State-wise).                                                                         (Para 19.3)
           The Committee welcomes the move of the Ministry to provide assistance for synthetic/wooden surfaces for
tennis, basketball, volleyball and squash in addition to hockey and athletic track but the Committee feels that
these projects should be completed in a stipulated timeframe. This proposal should be taken up by keeping in
mind the problems encountered earlier.                                                                                   (Para 19.4)
XX.   SCHEME RELATING TO INCENTIVES FOR PROMOTION OF SPORTS ACTIVITIES
        The Committee notes that during 2003-2004, BE allocation of Rs. 15.06 crores was reduced to Rs. 9.76
crores in RE. The Committee expresses its anguish over the reduction under such an important scheme having

152nd Report of Committee on HRD
file:///D/Committee%20on%20HRD/152ndreport.htm[01-07-2016 15:21:26]
varied components for promoting sports activity.                                                          (Para 20.1)
           The Committee finds that out of the five schemes, the financial performance in case of ‘sports scholarship
scheme’ and ‘pension for meritorious sports persons’ has been good. In the case of other three, things were not
that good. In the case of Rural sports programme, for example, there were variation in allocation in BE 2001-02
and 2002-03. BE, 2003-04 was reduced at RE Stage due to general cut in Ministry’s allocation. The Committee
notes that the impact of this cut was borne by this scheme meant for rural sports. Rural sports, the Committee
feels, are not getting the required attention.                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                           (Para 20.2)
           The Committee takes a serious view of the casual manner in which this scheme meant for the school games
is being implemented. The Committee strongly recommends that the Ministry should vigorously pursue
procurement of pending UCs and also try to simplify the procedure for it with a view to encouraging States to
come forward and send proposals.                                                                                            (Para 20.3)
           Similarly, National Sports Development Fund could not pick up due to poor response from
private/corporate units and individuals. As a result, provision in RE 2001-02, 2002-03 and 2003-04 had to be
reduced, as no matching grants were available. The Committee feels that with the present state of affairs, there
appears to be little hope from this scheme. The Ministry must therefore, revisit this scheme at the earliest.   (Para
20.4)
XXI.  SPECIAL AWARDS TO WINNERS IN INTERNATIONAL SPORTS EVENTS AND THEIR
           COACHES
           The Committee is of the opinion that the pension scheme for sportspersons is a good scheme but it needs to
be further streamlined and strengthened. Besides, the Committee suggests that other facilities like CGHS
benefits should also be extended to them. It has come to the notice of the Committee that many cases of
sportspersons for pension are pending. The  Committee would like the Ministry to expedite the
disposal of pension cases pending with it as early as possible.                                                                                (Para
21.3)
XXII.ASSISTANCE TO NATIONAL SPORTS FEDERATIONS
           The Committee is aware about questions being raised from different quarters particularly in media about
the functioning of National Sports Federations. While the Committee feels concerned about those
questions, it, however, thinks that National Sports Federations are the  lynchpin in the entire
sports structure of the country. Organisations like Indian Olympic Association are under certain
international obligations as well. While recognizing the key contribution of the NSFs in the promotion and
development of sports in the country, the Committee is of the opinion that they should also see that their
functioning does not leave any cause of complain. If some of the NSFs were not functioning in transparent
manner and the matter is reported in the newspaper, it does not mean that functioning  of all the
NSFs are questionable.           (Para 22.5)
        The  Committee feels that if the Ministry had initiated some steps to start a  dialogue on the
issues of concern, the NSFs including IOA should have  cooperated in this endeavour of the
Ministry. In present scenario, some  revolutionary decision needs to be taken to achieve results in a
fixed timeframe as has been done in other countries like China, South Korea and,  Taiwan. Such a
strategy could be chalked out only after the Ministry, the  Federations, IOA and the corporate
houses and all the stakeholders in sports sit together to share each other concerns and identified
the problems.                                                                                                                   (Para 22.6)
        The  Committee is happy to know that soon after the conclusion of the Commonwealth and the
Asian Games in 2002, the Ministry undertook the exercise of finalizing  Long Term Development
Plans with various NSFs. The exercise has been completed and a review undertaken in respect of
some of the Federations also.  The Committee would like to know the result of that review for its
knowledge.                                                                                               (Para 22.7)
        The  Committee would like to mention about the alleged non-submission of UCs by some
sports federations that has become a recurrent feature and the Ministry has not been able to tackle
the problem. Besides, statement of accounts is also not  being published by some sports federations.
The Committee would like the  Ministry to ensure the financial accountability of these federations.
The  Committee is surprised at the silence maintained by the Ministry on this aspect. This
approach ultimately would hamper the development of sports. The  Committee would like the

152nd Report of Committee on HRD
file:///D/Committee%20on%20HRD/152ndreport.htm[01-07-2016 15:21:26]
Ministry to adopt more pro-active approach in these  matters.                                     (Para 22.8)
XXIII.  STATE SPORTS ACADEMY
           The Committee feels that this scheme has not taken off at all mainly due to from poor response from
the corporate sector. The  Committee appreciates the efforts made by the Ministry to discuss the
problems with the private sector and based on discussions held so far the scheme has been proposed to be
revised. The Committee therefore, recommends that the process of revision be expedited as early as
possible.           (Para 23.3)
           The Committee calls upon the corporate houses to co-operate in this national endeavour as part of their
social responsibility. Any apprehensions/problems that they may be having in contributing for this noble cause,
the Committee feels, could be taken care of after mutual consultations with the Ministry as well as Federations. 
(Para 23.4)
XXIV.                                                                                                NORTH-EASTERN STATES
        North-Eastern States have been provided special emphasis by making separate provision for this
area both for the youth programmes as well as sports activities. These States have immense potential for sports
development and have produced many outstanding sportspersons who have brought laurels for the country.
Looking at the financial performance of the Ministry in this region, the Committee feels that these states didn’t
receive the attention they deserved. The Committee therefore, recommends to have a separate unit in the
Ministry to monitor the implementation of the schemes in this area and would like to have a status report after
every six months.                                                                                                             (Para 24.1)
XXV.  PROMOTION OF SPORTS AMONG DISABLED
           Under the scheme of Promotion of Sports among disabled a token provision of Rs. 4 lakh has been made
for BE 2004-05. The Committee is dismayed to observe that the scheme is being merged into the scheme relating
to events and the same is under formulation. This appears to be a strange move on the part of the Ministry. The
Committee recommends that the scheme of disabled should be finalized at the earliest and every possible steps be
taken to run it as a separate scheme.                                                                             (Para 25.2)
XXVI.MONITORING OF SCHEMES
           The Committee is surprised to see that there is no permanent mechanism in the Ministry of its own to
receive regular feedback as well as to monitor various programmes, both under Youth Welfare and the Sports.
This is an aspect without which, it is not possible to know about the performance and success of the schemes run
by the Ministry. The Committee was informed that monitoring was being done basically by two Committees one
formed under the DG, SAI and the other under the Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports. The Committee
disapproves a  monitoring activity which is so centralised that it is being done from the Centre. Sports being
the State subject, the Committee feels, any mechanism which is not from down-to-the-top is bound to be
ineffective. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should devise a decentralised mechanism of
monitoring of its schemes at the earliest.                                                                                          (Para 26.2)
